name: Dolomite legacy exchange callFunction approval drain
summary: The retired Ethereum Dolomite exchange contract exposes callFunction(), which performs an arbitrary external call on behalf of the contract. Its only protection is a noEntry reentrancy flag that the caller can clear by entering through the unguarded SoloMargin operate path, after which anyone can make the contract call transferFrom on any token. The attacker used it to pull USDC, WETH and DAI out of every wallet that still held a stale approval to the contract.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0x22a4299068aaddae4278d9cc934b84fc3905447f73bd4a54063beaceb72e344a both at the deployment block 10243378 and at block 19477008, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

Eleven transactions from the attacker EOA call the exchange contract between blocks 19477009 and 19477249; netting ERC-20 transfers across all eleven gives exactly these three tokens, with the attacker helper contract 0x0da9fcc650e2109e09344fd571bb78091b781f06 receiving essentially all of it and a few wei reaching 0x02c57952e2e406a9a9af2dff2c280c59df9a8b8b. Losses fall on the individual approval-granting wallets, not on protocol-held funds. Contemporaneous reporting put the loss near USD 1.8 million. Nothing was recovered.
